# AppShell

The frame of an application: a top bar, a sidebar (usually a Nav) and the main area. It fills the viewport; the
main area and the sidebar scroll on their own. Every application needs it exactly once, around its pages.

**Interaction**: a skip link ("Skip to content") is the first focusable element and moves the focus to the main
area. AppShell.Toggle collapses the sidebar to icons on wide layouts (controlled with `collapsed` and
`onCollapsedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultCollapsed`). Below 960 px of width (a narrow page next to the
narrowest sidebar), the sidebar becomes a drawer over the content: AppShell.Toggle opens it, focus moves to the
current item and stays inside, and `Esc`, a click outside or choosing a Nav item close it and return the focus.
The main area has `view-transition-name: vl-main`, so the page transition of `vellum-ui/global.css` works
without CSS of your own. Landmarks: `header`, the `nav` of Nav, `main`.

**Category**: Patterns · **Common uses**: The root of an application: top bar, sidebar navigation and the page

## Import

```ts
import { AppShell } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

The header holds AppShell.Toggle, the name of the application and the account; the sidebar holds a Nav; the
page goes in the children. The sidebar collapses to icons with the toggle, and becomes a drawer when the frame
is narrower than 960 px. `contained` keeps the example inside this page: an application leaves it out, so that
the frame fills the window.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import {
  AppShell,
  Avatar,
  Button,
  IconButton,
  ListItem,
  Nav,
  type NavGroup,
  type NavItem,
  Page,
  Panel,
  Spacer,
  Stack,
  Text,
} from 'vellum-ui'

const ITEMS: readonly (NavItem | NavGroup)[] = [
  { key: 'home', label: 'Home', icon: 'home' },
  { key: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', icon: 'inbox', count: 4, countTone: 'accent' },
  { key: 'projects', label: 'Projects', icon: 'folder' },
  {
    type: 'group',
    label: 'Workspace',
    items: [
      { key: 'members', label: 'Members', icon: 'users' },
      { key: 'reports', label: 'Reports', icon: 'chart' },
      { key: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: 'settings' },
    ],
  },
]

const TITLES: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  home: 'Home',
  inbox: 'Inbox',
  projects: 'Projects',
  members: 'Members',
  reports: 'Reports',
  settings: 'Settings',
}

export function Basic() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState('inbox')
  return (
    <AppShell
      contained
      header={
        <>
          <AppShell.Toggle />
          <Text weight="semibold">Acme</Text>
          <Spacer />
          <IconButton icon="bell" label="Notifications" />
          <Avatar name="Alex Morgan" size={28} />
        </>
      }
      sidebar={<Nav items={ITEMS} value={page} onSelect={setPage} />}
    >
      <Page
        title={TITLES[page] ?? page}
        subtitle="Everything that needs your attention"
        actions={<Button variant="primary">New project</Button>}
      >
        <Panel flush>
          <Stack gap={1} padding={2}>
            <ListItem title="Quarterly review" description="Due on Friday" onClick={() => {}} />
            <ListItem title="Website refresh" description="3 open tasks" onClick={() => {}} />
            <ListItem title="Onboarding guide" description="Draft" onClick={() => {}} />
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
      </Page>
    </AppShell>
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Full-screen interface

`flush` removes the padding of the main area, for interfaces whose root is a flush SplitView, such as a chat.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import {
  AppShell,
  EmptyState,
  ListItem,
  Nav,
  type NavGroup,
  type NavItem,
  SplitView,
  Stack,
  Text,
} from 'vellum-ui'

const ITEMS: readonly (NavItem | NavGroup)[] = [
  { key: 'home', label: 'Home', icon: 'home' },
  { key: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', icon: 'inbox', count: 4, countTone: 'accent' },
  { key: 'projects', label: 'Projects', icon: 'folder' },
  {
    type: 'group',
    label: 'Workspace',
    items: [
      { key: 'members', label: 'Members', icon: 'users' },
      { key: 'reports', label: 'Reports', icon: 'chart' },
      { key: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: 'settings' },
    ],
  },
]

export function FullScreen() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState('inbox')
  return (
    <AppShell
      contained
      flush
      defaultCollapsed
      header={
        <>
          <AppShell.Toggle />
          <Text weight="semibold">Acme</Text>
        </>
      }
      sidebar={<Nav items={ITEMS} value={page} onSelect={setPage} />}
    >
      <SplitView
        variant="flush"
        aside={
          <Stack gap={1} padding={2}>
            <ListItem title="Design team" description="See you at 3" selected onClick={() => {}} />
            <ListItem title="Jordan Lee" description="Thanks!" onClick={() => {}} />
          </Stack>
        }
      >
        <EmptyState icon="messages" title="Design team" description="Messages appear here" fill />
      </SplitView>
    </AppShell>
  )
}
```

## Advanced

### Controlled collapse with a shortcut

Keep `collapsed` in your state to save it or to change it from elsewhere, such as with the `[` key. AppShell.Toggle
calls `onCollapsedChange`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { AppShell, Kbd, Nav, type NavGroup, type NavItem, Page, Text, useHotkeys } from 'vellum-ui'

const ITEMS: readonly (NavItem | NavGroup)[] = [
  { key: 'home', label: 'Home', icon: 'home' },
  { key: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', icon: 'inbox', count: 4, countTone: 'accent' },
  { key: 'projects', label: 'Projects', icon: 'folder' },
  {
    type: 'group',
    label: 'Workspace',
    items: [
      { key: 'members', label: 'Members', icon: 'users' },
      { key: 'reports', label: 'Reports', icon: 'chart' },
      { key: 'settings', label: 'Settings', icon: 'settings' },
    ],
  },
]

const TITLES: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  home: 'Home',
  inbox: 'Inbox',
  projects: 'Projects',
  members: 'Members',
  reports: 'Reports',
  settings: 'Settings',
}

export function Controlled() {
  const [collapsed, setCollapsed] = useState(true)
  const [page, setPage] = useState('home')
  useHotkeys('[', () => setCollapsed((c) => !c), { description: 'Collapse or expand the sidebar' })
  return (
    <AppShell
      contained
      collapsed={collapsed}
      onCollapsedChange={setCollapsed}
      header={
        <>
          <AppShell.Toggle />
          <Text weight="semibold">Acme</Text>
        </>
      }
      sidebar={<Nav items={ITEMS} value={page} onSelect={setPage} />}
    >
      <Page title={TITLES[page] ?? page}>
        <Text tone="secondary">
          Press <Kbd keys="[" /> to collapse or expand the sidebar.
        </Text>
      </Page>
    </AppShell>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | `ReactNode` | Content of the top bar, laid out in a row with step 3 gaps: usually AppShell.Toggle, the name of the application, a Spacer, then search and the account menu. Rendered in a `header` landmark. | — | No |
| `sidebar` | `ReactNode` | Content of the sidebar, usually a Nav; it scrolls on its own. A Nav inside follows the collapsed state. | — | No |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The page, rendered in the `main` landmark, which scrolls on its own; usually a Page. | — | No |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | Collapsed sidebar (controlled): icons only. Applies to wide layouts; on narrow ones, the sidebar is a drawer that is closed until AppShell.Toggle opens it. | — | No |
| `defaultCollapsed` | `boolean` | Initial collapsed state (uncontrolled). | `false` | No |
| `onCollapsedChange` | `(collapsed: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state when AppShell.Toggle collapses or expands the sidebar of a wide layout. | — | No |
| `sidebarWidth` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | Width step of the expanded sidebar: `sm` 240, `md` 280, `lg` 320 px (the widths of SplitView). | `'sm'` | No |
| `flush` | `boolean` | Main area without padding, for full-screen interfaces (a chat, image viewing) whose root is a flush SplitView. | — | No |
| `contained` | `boolean` | Fills its container instead of the viewport: for an application inside a frame, a preview or an example. | — | No |
| `mainId` | `string` | `id` of the `main` element, the target of the skip link; generated when omitted. | — | No |
| `testId` | `string` | Test id, rendered as `data-testid`. | — | No |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.

## AppShell.Toggle

The button that shows or hides the sidebar, to place in the header (usually first) or anywhere inside
AppShell: on wide layouts it collapses and expands the sidebar ("Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar"), on
narrow ones it opens the sidebar drawer ("Open navigation"). It is an IconButton with `aria-expanded` and
`aria-controls`; outside AppShell it renders nothing.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `testId` | `string` | Test id, rendered as `data-testid`. | — | No |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
